label: Luau
host: Rust 1.99.1 (mlua (features luau, vendored) 0.12.2, release, fat LTO)
notes: A session builds the whole engine (nothing shared between sessions), applies its limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust. Limits: Lua::new() (ALL_SAFE libs), sandbox(true), set_interrupt (returns Continue), set_memory_limit(64MiB).
Memory: resident growth across 1,000 live sessions (stopped by target), measured first in a fresh process.

Tool call: the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack. Median of per-batch means, 1,000,000 calls in batches of 1,000 after 100,000 warm-ups; mean 2.0429 µs, slowest batch 3.5924 µs per call; 2.0414 µs of CPU per call.
Session = Lua::new() + memory limit + interrupt + global call + sandbox(true); call is registered before sandbox(true) so it sits in the read-only globals.
Host fn is lua.create_function(|lua, Table| -> Table); fields read with Table::get and the reply built with create_table_with_capacity(0, 3), mirroring the C harness's lua_getfield/lua_setfield.

Secondary measurements in the same session (sandbox kept): after remove_interrupt() toolCallWallUs=1.9697, toolCallCpuUs=2.0029; after also set_memory_limit(0) toolCallWallUs=0.6374, toolCallCpuUs=0.6426 (1,000,000 calls each). With a memory limit set, mlua runs each allocating table operation (create_table, set) as a protected call so an allocation failure cannot unwind through Rust.

Luau allocates GC objects from per-size-class pages, so a fresh mlua Luau state reports about 436 KB from Lua::used_memory(), of which about 182 KB is resident before our call function, limits, and sandbox are added (separate diagnostic in diag/luau-mem, 1,000 states).
Compute: not measured in the Rust host.
